newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreigners, futures up S.Africa stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners, futures up S.Africa stocks.

text.p: Strong foreign buying and futures-driven trade hoisted South African shares to new highs, pushing the all-share index above the 7,600 level for the first time in big turnover trade.

Dealers said the weaker rand, which tumbled to its lowest level in seven months, drew offshore interest as shares became cheaper for overseas investors. Rand hedges and gold stocks also gained on some local concerns about the currency.
Futures-related basket trades and asset swaps also drove the market to turnover of around 1.9 billion rand -- more than double an average day's takings.
Stronger world markets added momentum to the local market as did expectations for a local interest rate cut.
The industrial index added 67.1 points to a new closing high of 9,314.2 lifting the all-share to a fresh closing peak of 9,314.2 -- a gain of 67.6 points.
Gold shares were overshadowed by positive activity on the gold board, adding 10.1 points to close at 967.1.
